title: Finite-presentation closed envelopes for quasi-affine locally finite type maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. A morphism is quasi-affine if it is representable by schemes and every pullback along an affine scheme test is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. A closed immersion is representable by schemes and a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $g:A\to B$ be a locally finite type quasi-affine morphism and suppose $B$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exist an algebraic space $C$, a closed immersion $e:A\hookrightarrow C$, and a morphism of finite presentation $v:C\to B$ such that $v\circ e=g$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-quasiaffine-affine-factorization], factor $g$ as $A\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}B$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ affine. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], $Z$ is qcqs. The source $A$ is quasi-compact: pull $j$ back along a quasi-compact etale atlas of $Z$; quasi-compactness of $j$ makes its source quasi-compact, and that source is an atlas of $A$. Here the tests on quasi-compact spaces are supplied by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local].

By [lem-sfb-space-affine-fp-limit], write $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ over $B$, indexed by a small nonempty directed set, with affine transitions and each $Z_i\to B$ affine and finitely presented. Every $Z_i$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. Regard $A$ as its open image in $Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-limit-open-cover-descent] to the two-member covering family $A,Z$ of $Z$. It yields a stage $i_0$ and a quasi-compact open $U_{i_0}\subset Z_{i_0}$ with $Z\times_{Z_{i_0}}U_{i_0}=A$. The second member of the covering is only to meet that lemma's covering hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0871, approximation and descent of the open; Tags 0870 and 0827

proof.text: For $i\ge i_0$ set $U_i=Z_i\times_{Z_{i_0}}U_{i_0}$. The inverse images are quasi-compact and quasi-separated and have affine transitions by the last clause of [lem-sfb-space-limit-open-cover-descent], applied to the descended two-member covering. The sheaf limit of this system is $A$: for every test scheme $T$, a compatible tuple in the $U_i(T)$ is exactly a compatible tuple in the $Z_i(T)$ whose $i_0$ component belongs to $U_{i_0}(T)$. These are precisely $(Z\times_{Z_{i_0}}U_{i_0})(T)=A(T)$. The tail $i\ge i_0$ has the same limit since it is cofinal in the directed set.

source.place: Tag 0871, sentence defining the inverse images U_i; pointwise sheaf-limit verification

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-eventual-closed-immersion] with common base $B$, inverse system $(U_i)_{i\ge i_0}$, source $A$, and closed immersion $\mathrm{id}_A:A\to\varprojlim U_i=A$. Its stages are quasi-compact by the previous step, its transitions affine, and $A\to B$ is the given locally finite type map $g$. Thus for some $i\ge i_0$ the projection $e:A\to U_i$ is a closed immersion.

The open inclusion $k:U_i\hookrightarrow Z_i$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], since $U_i$ is quasi-compact and $Z_i$ quasi-separated. It is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-qc-open-finite-presentation]. Therefore $v:U_i\xrightarrow{k}Z_i\to B$ is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Put $C=U_i$. Every projection in the constructed inverse system is a $B$-map, so $v\circ e=g$. This gives all the required data.
